policy: SQL drivers and PgPool are forbidden in policy layers unless a path is listed here with a removal step.

allowlist.reason: Current identity SSOT performs credential, lockout, role, and membership SQL directly.
Refresh-token and API-key persistence is selected inside the API policy service.
API-key lifecycle still reaches PostgreSQL-specific persistence paths from handlers.
Workspace, tenant, membership, quota, and metrics policy owns a PgPool and direct SQL.
Conversation policy is constructed directly from PgPool instead of ConversationStorage.
Workspace document indexing and lookup use direct relational queries in an API service.
Document list/read merge policy executes PostgreSQL queries instead of a scoped document reader port.
Queue policy reads and mutates task relational state outside the task adapter.
Task/document synchronization performs direct PostgreSQL updates across service boundaries.
The process-global sidecar pool provides direct SQL access to policy services.
Ingestion staging mirrors document state with direct PostgreSQL statements.
Admission idempotency and dedup state are implemented as direct SQL in policy code.
Pipeline checkpoint persistence is coupled to PostgreSQL instead of an injected checkpoint port.
Artifact metadata lookup includes direct PostgreSQL access and provider-specific absence handling.
Multimodal manifest/chunk policy persists and loads PostgreSQL rows directly.
PDF lineage persistence is direct PostgreSQL SQL outside the blob adapter traits.
Runtime server configuration persistence uses PostgreSQL-specific storage in the API layer.
The relational entity sink is assembled in the API crate and exposes PostgreSQL transaction details.
Graph lineage authority writes are implemented in an API-local PostgreSQL sink.
Projection delivery policy currently consumes PostgreSQL outbox details directly.
